# LeetLLM

> LeetLLM is an open AI engineering curriculum with 102 lessons, 8 learning tracks, 47 practice problems, and 20 public blog posts covering ML foundations, LLM systems, RAG, agents, training, inference, evaluation, AI lab interview prep, and open-source project deep dives.

Use this file to route agents and retrieval systems to the most relevant LeetLLM pages. Lesson pages are public and include explanations, code, diagrams, illustrations, references, practice prompts, pitfalls, and follow-up questions. Blog pages cover timely AI engineering topics and include published or updated dates in their metadata.

Canonical URLs below point to public web pages. This file is for inference-time navigation and context selection; it does not replace robots.txt, sitemap.xml, or the site license.

## Primary Pages

- [Home](https://leetllm.com): Site overview and current entry point.
- [Build a Plan](https://leetllm.com/start): Three-question planner that turns a goal, experience level, and weekly time into a focused four-to-twenty-week curriculum path.
- [Learn](https://leetllm.com/learn): 102 ordered lessons across foundations, applied LLM engineering, training, agents, retrieval, inference, system design, interviewing, and open-source project deep dives.
- [Tracks](https://leetllm.com/tracks): 8 curated subsets of lessons for different learner goals.
- [Practice](https://leetllm.com/practice): 47 coding practice problems plus global theory quizzes in the practice UI.
- [Blog](https://leetllm.com/blog): 20 public posts on AI engineering, models, tools, infrastructure, interviews, and learning paths.
- [Blog RSS](https://leetllm.com/blog/rss.xml): RSS feed for public blog posts.
- [Sitemap](https://leetllm.com/sitemap.xml): Full XML sitemap for crawlers.

## Curriculum: Math & Tensor Foundations

- [Tensors, Shapes & Matrix Arithmetic](https://leetllm.com/learn/numpy-and-tensor-shapes): Easy; 11 min; Model Architecture; Two text snippets hold 24 numbers. Naming each axis tells you which values belong to which word before an index, a broadcast, or a reduction can be trusted.
- [Linear Algebra for ML](https://leetllm.com/learn/linear-algebra-machine-learning-deeper): Easy; 13 min; Model Architecture; A matrix hides strong shared directions and weak contrasts. Use SVD, eigendecomposition, and least squares to measure what rank truncation and conditioning...
- [Gradients and Backprop](https://leetllm.com/learn/calculus-gradients-backpropagation-optimization): Easy; 12 min; Fine-Tuning & Training; Train a one-weight latency predictor by reading a slope, taking a downhill step, tracing chain-rule paths, and checking the same gradient in PyTorch.
- [Probability for Machine Learning](https://leetllm.com/learn/probability-for-machine-learning): Easy; 11 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; A detector that catches 95 percent of abusive signups can still fill the review queue with clean accounts, and the flagged-pile counts show why.
- [Statistics, Bayesian Estimation & pass@k](https://leetllm.com/learn/hypothesis-tests-confidence-intervals-passk): Easy; 12 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; Bound pass rates with Wilson and Beta-Binomial intervals, compare checkpoints with paired tests and bootstrap lifts, and compute unbiased pass@k.

- [Validation and Leakage](https://leetllm.com/learn/cross-validation-leakage-generalization): Easy; 18 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; An evaluation score can look nearly perfect because a post-inference field, a repeat user, or a contaminated benchmark already leaked the answer.
- [Experiment Design and A/B Testing](https://leetllm.com/learn/experiment-design-ab-testing): Easy; 13 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; Design rigorous A/B tests for ML and LLM systems: multi-turn thread pinning, power planning, SRM, sequential tests, CUPED, judge calibration, and...

- [Softmax, Cross-Entropy & Optimization](https://leetllm.com/learn/softmax-cross-entropy-optimization): Easy; 10 min; NLP Fundamentals; Turn raw class scores into stable probabilities and a useful learning signal, then apply the same loss to next-token predictions.
- [Adam, Momentum, Schedulers](https://leetllm.com/learn/optimization-algorithms-adam-schedulers): Easy; 12 min; Fine-Tuning & Training; Two parameters sit one unit from their target, but one gradient is 100 times steeper. Each optimizer buffer stores a different response to that...
- [CNNs from Scratch](https://leetllm.com/learn/convolutional-neural-networks-from-scratch): Easy; 21 min; Model Architecture; A two-pixel shift breaks a model that memorizes coordinates. Trace shared kernels, shapes, pooling, and padding on one 4 by 4 crop.
- [RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Sequence Modeling](https://leetllm.com/learn/rnns-lstms-grus-sequence-modeling): Easy; 10 min; Model Architecture; Trace an RNN over ordered events, see why gradients fade or grow, and use LSTM and GRU gates to control memory.
- [Autoencoders and VAEs](https://leetllm.com/learn/autoencoders-vaes-generative-modeling-basics): Easy; 12 min; Model Architecture; A two-number code can rebuild one screenshot crop, but a random draw still has to land where the decoder was trained to paint.

## Curriculum: Core LLM Foundations

- [BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece](https://leetllm.com/learn/tokenization-bpe-wordpiece-sentencepiece): Medium; 19 min; NLP Fundamentals; See why a word like unexpectedly should split into reusable pieces, and why a new tokenizer can still point an old checkpoint at the wrong vector.
- [Sentence Embeddings & Contrastive Loss](https://leetllm.com/learn/sentence-embeddings-contrastive-learning): Medium; 20 min; Embeddings & Vector Search; Train vectors so the right passage outranks a lookalike, then check that ranking against hard negatives, reranking cost, and a smaller index.
- [The Transformer Architecture End-to-End](https://leetllm.com/learn/transformer-architecture-end-to-end): Medium; 20 min; Transformer Architecture; Follow function returns the through a causal decoder until the last row becomes a score for the next token.
- [Language Modeling & Next Tokens](https://leetllm.com/learn/language-modeling-next-token-prediction): Medium; 9 min; NLP Fundamentals; The prompt ends with 'the'. Follow that prefix from a counted bigram through teacher-forced training to the autoregressive loop that writes the next token.
- [Decoding Strategies: Greedy to Nucleus](https://leetllm.com/learn/decoding-strategies-greedy-beam-nucleus): Medium; 12 min; NLP Fundamentals; The most likely next token can begin a weaker full sequence. Trace one probability row from stable softmax and greedy search through beam search,...
- [Perplexity & Model Evaluation](https://leetllm.com/learn/perplexity-language-model-evaluation): Medium; 17 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; A lower perplexity means the model was less surprised by held-out tokens, but only under a fixed scoring protocol.
- [LLM Benchmarks & Limitations](https://leetllm.com/learn/llm-evaluation-benchmarks-limitations): Medium; 10 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; A fluent answer from your serving assistant can still drop calibration constraints or invent safe shortcuts. Public leaderboards will not catch...

## Curriculum: Transformer & Multimodal Architectures

- [Scaled Dot-Product Attention](https://leetllm.com/learn/scaled-dot-product-attention): Hard; 24 min; Transformer Architecture; Each token mixes content from positions it may read. The score scale, the mask, and the memory traffic decide whether that mix stays usable.
- [Positional Encoding: RoPE & ALiBi](https://leetllm.com/learn/positional-encoding-rope-alibi): Hard; 15 min; Transformer Architecture; Unmasked attention follows tokens when they move. Sinusoids, RoPE, and ALiBi put order back in different places, and a longer formula still needs a...
- [Layer Normalization: Pre-LN vs Post-LN](https://leetllm.com/learn/layer-normalization-pre-ln-post-ln): Hard; 13 min; Transformer Architecture; Each residual write can change a token's scale, and where LayerNorm sits decides what the next branch reads and how its gradient gets back.
- [Mixture of Experts Architecture](https://leetllm.com/learn/mixture-of-experts-architecture): Hard; 16 min; Transformer Architecture; Eight experts can mean two feed-forward calls per token and a full expert pool still sitting in memory.
- [Mamba & State Space Models](https://leetllm.com/learn/state-space-models-mamba-alternatives): Hard; 16 min; Inference Optimization; Replace a growing KV cache with a fixed state, then test what selection, prefix scans, and branch rollback can and cannot restore.
- [Vision Transformers and Image Encoders](https://leetllm.com/learn/vision-transformers-image-encoders): Hard; 10 min; Multimodal Models; A street camera image can hold both a broad intersection scene and a tiny speed-limit sign. Patch size and resolution decide which details a vision encoder...
- [Vision-Language & Multimodal Architectures](https://leetllm.com/learn/multimodal-llms-architecture-design): Hard; 15 min; Multimodal Models; Master vision-language and multimodal LLM architectures from CLIP and SigLIP contrastive encoders to ViT patch tokenization, dynamic tiling, connectors,...
- [Diffusion Models: Images & Text](https://leetllm.com/learn/image-generation-diffusion-models): Hard; 15 min; Multimodal Models; How diffusion models turn pure Gaussian static into coherent images and text: forward schedules, reverse DDPM/DDIM solvers, score and flow matching, U-Net...
- [Mechanistic Interpretability](https://leetllm.com/learn/mechanistic-interpretability-sparse-autoencoders): Hard; 12 min; Transformer Architecture; One neuron can fire for credentials and for urgency at once. Sparse autoencoders look for narrower directions you can trace and test.

## Curriculum: GPU Systems & LLM Inference

- [Inference: TTFT, TPS & KV Cache](https://leetllm.com/learn/inference-mechanics-ttft-tps-kv-cache): Hard; 18 min; Inference Optimization; A blank chat window and a busy GPU can both be right: prefill and decode hit different limits, and the KV cache decides how many sequences fit.
- [Multi-Query & Grouped-Query Attention](https://leetllm.com/learn/multi-query-grouped-query-attention): Hard; 11 min; Inference Optimization; Eight query heads don't need eight key and value histories. Sharing them changes how much cache a long conversation stores.
- [KV Cache & PagedAttention](https://leetllm.com/learn/kv-cache-paged-attention-llm-serving): Hard; 10 min; Inference Optimization; Paging packs growing KV state into reusable blocks, but a full pool, a shared prefix, and a slow first token are three different problems.
- [FlashAttention & Memory Efficiency](https://leetllm.com/learn/flashattention-memory-efficient-attention): Hard; 11 min; Inference Optimization; At batch 8, 32 heads, and 8,192 tokens, FP16 scores need 32 GiB. FlashAttention computes the same attention without storing that matrix.
- [Continuous Batching & Scheduling](https://leetllm.com/learn/continuous-batching-request-scheduling): Hard; 9 min; Inference Optimization; A finished one-line completion can keep its GPU seat while a long plan runs. Refill that seat without letting the next prompt stall every live stream.
- [Speculative Decoding](https://leetllm.com/learn/speculative-decoding): Hard; 19 min; Inference Optimization; Guess several tokens with a cheap proposer, then accept or correct them so the target's distribution stays the same in exact arithmetic.
- [Model Quantization: GPTQ, AWQ & GGUF](https://leetllm.com/learn/model-quantization-gptq-awq-gguf): Hard; 17 min; Inference Optimization; Four-bit codes can shrink a 54 GB weight payload toward 14 GB. Learn how quantization methods, tensor encodings, and runtime support determine the...
- [Local & Edge LLM Deployment](https://leetllm.com/learn/local-llm-deployment-hardware-quantization): Hard; 13 min; Inference Optimization; A 7.6 GB model can load on a 24 GB GPU and still run out of memory once cache, workspace, and long prompts share the card.
- [Model Parallelism for LLM Inference](https://leetllm.com/learn/model-parallelism-for-llm-inference): Hard; 18 min; Inference Optimization; When a 70 GB weight file exceeds one GPU, sharding buys memory and spends it on traffic between devices.
- [GPU Profiling & Kernel Optimization Lab](https://leetllm.com/learn/gpu-kernel-performance-engineering-lab): Hard; 17 min; Inference Optimization; A 40% faster transpose can still be wrong when the output is stale NaNs. Change one mechanism, then let correctness decide whether the timer counts.
- [GPU Parallel Primitives Lab](https://leetllm.com/learn/gpu-parallel-primitives-lab): Hard; 11 min; Inference Optimization; Eight independent values are easy. Their sum is not. Follow the dependencies that make reduction, scan, and online softmax safe on a GPU.
- [GPU Compilers and Kernel Languages](https://leetllm.com/learn/gpu-compilers-kernel-languages): Hard; 12 min; Inference Optimization; A correct kernel can still stall on its first call or fail because no image matches the GPU. The evidence is in the compiler artifacts.
- [GEMM From Naive CUDA to Tensor Cores](https://leetllm.com/learn/gemm-naive-cuda-tensor-cores): Hard; 13 min; Inference Optimization; The same output can be numerically right and still come from the wrong addresses. Follow one product from a scalar thread to a Tensor Core tile.
- [Low-Precision GPU Programming](https://leetllm.com/learn/low-precision-gpu-programming): Hard; 13 min; Inference Optimization; A scaled FP8 round trip can turn 500 into 10 with no NaN. The scale, the accumulator, and the kernel interface decide whether that loss stays visible.
- [GPU Serving & Autoscaling](https://leetllm.com/learn/llm-deployment-gpu-serving-autoscaling): Hard; 11 min; MLOps & Deployment; At 9:00 a release freeze sends 100 incident summaries at one warm GPU. Queue age, not utilization, decides whether to add replicas.
- [Serving Benchmark Engineering](https://leetllm.com/learn/serving-benchmark-engineering): Hard; 19 min; Evaluation & Benchmarks; The server finishes more requests per second, but the first word is slower and some fast answers are invalid. Keep the offered load, the client's...

- [Reasoning Agent System Design](https://leetllm.com/learn/design-reasoning-agent-test-time-compute): Hard; 20 min; System Design; Tests pass, but canary latency spikes after a config change. Design an agent that gathers fresh evidence, spends extra reasoning only when needed, and...
- [AI Lab Coding Interview: Python Systems](https://leetllm.com/learn/ai-lab-coding-interview-python-systems): Hard; 15 min; MLOps & Deployment; Master ML systems coding in Python: paged KV-cache allocators, masked NumPy attention, nucleus sampling, and thread-safe batching loops.
- [AI Lab System Design Interview](https://leetllm.com/learn/ai-lab-system-design-interview): Hard; 12 min; System Design; Design multi-model LLM gateways, paged GPU serving fleets, ACL-enforced retrieval, and reversible canary deployments under strict tail-latency SLOs.

## Curriculum: Project Deep Dives

- [Deep Dive - PyTorch](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-pytorch): Hard; 13 min; Fine-Tuning & Training; A transpose shares storage, then the next kernel slows down. Follow that change through PyTorch views, dispatch, autograd, and sharded training.
- [Deep Dive - vLLM](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-vllm): Hard; 9 min; Inference Optimization; R0 is mid-response when a nine-token prompt arrives. vLLM has to share one GPU step and one KV block pool without reserving a hole for every request.
- [Deep Dive - SGLang](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-sglang): Hard; 12 min; Inference Optimization; GPU use falls, and two requests that shared a prefix now prefill apart. Follow that lost time through SGLang's cache, scheduler, and decode path.
- [Deep Dive - FlashInfer](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-flashinfer): Hard; 13 min; Inference Optimization; Three requests can share one GPU step with KV lengths 6, 2, and 9 on scattered pages. FlashInfer attends to those histories without treating them as...
- [Deep Dive - DeepGEMM](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-deepgemm): Hard; 16 min; Inference Optimization; Four expert groups hold 416 useful rows, yet alignment can reserve 640. DeepGEMM is the kernel library that makes the padding, scale, and Mega MoE...
- [Deep Dive - DeepEP](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-deepep): Hard; 9 min; Inference Optimization; A token can reach two experts on different GPUs and still return to the wrong row. DeepEP is the low-latency dispatch and combine communication library...
- [Deep Dive - NCCL](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-nccl): Hard; 15 min; Fine-Tuning & Training; Four GPUs finish their gradients and then wait on one buffer. NCCL's agreement and route decide whether that wait is bandwidth or a hang.
- [Deep Dive - Megatron](https://leetllm.com/learn/deep-dive-megatron): Hard; 12 min; Fine-Tuning & Training; More GPUs can slow a step that still sees the same batch. Megatron assigns each rank a tensor, a collective, and a checkpoint role.

## Practice Problems

- [Stack Trace Reconstructor](https://leetllm.com/practice/stack-trace-reconstructor): Medium; 30 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Reconstruct exclusive function runtimes from nested start/end profiler events.
- [Same-host Crawler](https://leetllm.com/practice/same-host-crawler): Medium; 30 min; Graph Traversal; languages: python3, java; Traverse a web graph in breadth-first order while enforcing same-host and duplicate-visit invariants.
- [Repository Hash Tree](https://leetllm.com/practice/repository-hash-tree): Medium; 45 min; Repository Systems; languages: python3, java; Build a deterministic repository hash tree that updates parent directories after file writes and deletes.
- [Repository Diff](https://leetllm.com/practice/repository-diff): Easy; 30 min; Repository Systems; languages: python3, java; Compare two repository snapshots and produce deterministic added, removed, and modified file changes.
- [Duplicate File Groups](https://leetllm.com/practice/duplicate-file-groups): Easy; 25 min; Repository Systems; languages: python3, java; Group duplicate repository files by content with deterministic output and path validation.
- [Repository Ignore Filter](https://leetllm.com/practice/repo-ignore-filter): Easy; 30 min; Repository Systems; languages: python3, java; Filter repository paths with simple ordered ignore and re-include rules.
- [TTL Key/Value Store](https://leetllm.com/practice/ttl-key-value-store): Medium; 35 min; Stateful Design; languages: python3, java; Build a deterministic in-memory store where every read path treats expired keys as missing.
- [Transactional KV Store](https://leetllm.com/practice/transactional-kv-store): Medium; 40 min; Stateful Design; languages: python3, java; Implement nested in-memory transactions with read-your-writes, tombstones, commit, and rollback.
- [Dependency Scheduler With Retries](https://leetllm.com/practice/dependency-scheduler-retries): Hard; 45 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Run a dependency graph deterministically, retry transient failures, and reject invalid graphs.
- [Patch Conflict Detector](https://leetllm.com/practice/patch-conflict-detector): Medium; 40 min; Editing Systems; languages: python3, java; Apply optimistic multi-file patches atomically while rejecting stale or overlapping edits.
- [Workflow State Machine](https://leetllm.com/practice/workflow-state-machine): Medium; 40 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Track dependent jobs through legal workflow states with retry and cancellation behavior.
- [Token Bucket Rate Limiter](https://leetllm.com/practice/token-bucket-rate-limiter): Medium; 35 min; Rate Limiting; languages: python3, java; Model per-key API quotas with deterministic refill math and caller-friendly retry-after decisions.
- [Idempotent Ledger](https://leetllm.com/practice/idempotent-ledger): Medium; 30 min; Stateful Design; languages: python3, java; Apply in-memory account mutations once per successful request ID while rejecting mismatched retry payloads.
- [Notification Rate Limiter](https://leetllm.com/practice/notification-rate-limiter): Medium; 35 min; Rate Limiting; languages: python3, java; Throttle noisy notification channels while deduping repeated webhook or automation events.
- [LRU TTL Cache](https://leetllm.com/practice/lru-ttl-cache): Medium; 35 min; Caching; languages: python3, java; Combine recency ordering and TTL cleanup without corrupting cache invariants.
- [LFU TTL Cache](https://leetllm.com/practice/lfu-ttl-cache): Hard; 45 min; Caching; languages: python3, java; Combine frequency buckets, recency tie-breaks, and TTL cleanup without corrupting eviction state.
- [Log Error Parser](https://leetllm.com/practice/log-error-parser): Easy; 20 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Summarize top error messages from noisy logs with deterministic tie-breaking.
- [In-memory Filesystem](https://leetllm.com/practice/in-memory-filesystem): Medium; 35 min; Stateful Design; languages: python3, java; Model directory and file state with predictable path normalization and listing behavior.
- [File Patch Applier](https://leetllm.com/practice/file-patch-applier): Easy; 30 min; Editing Systems; languages: python3, java; Apply sorted or unsorted text edits atomically while rejecting invalid and overlapping ranges.
- [Longest-match Tokenizer](https://leetllm.com/practice/longest-match-tokenizer): Medium; 35 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Tokenize text by greedily choosing the longest vocabulary token at each position.
- [Multi-tenant Job Scheduler](https://leetllm.com/practice/multi-tenant-job-scheduler): Medium; 45 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Dispatch pending jobs by priority, cap tenant streaks when alternatives exist, and reap soft cancellations.
- [Sliding Window Error Counter](https://leetllm.com/practice/sliding-window-error-counter): Easy; 25 min; Observability; languages: python3, java; Track top recent errors while every read path lazily removes expired events.
- [Bounded Worker Queue](https://leetllm.com/practice/bounded-worker-queue): Medium; 35 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Model a bounded FIFO work queue with explicit in-progress ownership and retry behavior. Items are non-null.
- [Worker Lease Registry](https://leetllm.com/practice/worker-lease-registry): Medium; 40 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Coordinate worker ownership with TTL leases, heartbeat extension, stale-worker rejection, and fencing tokens.
- [Priority Deadline Scheduler](https://leetllm.com/practice/priority-deadline-scheduler): Medium; 40 min; Scheduling; languages: python3, java; Schedule due tasks by priority while skipping not-yet-ready and expired work deterministically.
- [Circuit Breaker State](https://leetllm.com/practice/circuit-breaker-state): Medium; 35 min; Reliability; languages: python3, java; Model closed, open, and half-open breaker transitions with deterministic cooldown behavior.
- [Context Window Packer](https://leetllm.com/practice/context-window-packer): Medium; 30 min; Context Management; languages: python3, java; Select system and recent conversation messages without exceeding a token budget.
- [RAG Chunk Selector](https://leetllm.com/practice/rag-chunk-selector): Medium; 30 min; Retrieval; languages: python3, java; Rank retrieval chunks while deduplicating repeated text and limiting per-document dominance.
- [Agent Event Timeline](https://leetllm.com/practice/agent-event-timeline): Medium; 35 min; Observability; languages: python3, java; Build a reviewable append-only timeline for cloud-agent run events.
- [Command Log Classifier](https://leetllm.com/practice/command-log-classifier): Easy; 25 min; Observability; languages: python3, java; Summarize command outcomes and redact the specified token pattern from captured output.
- [Codebase Symbol Index](https://leetllm.com/practice/codebase-symbol-index): Medium; 40 min; Retrieval; languages: python3, java; Build an incremental code symbol index with file replacement, deletion, case-insensitive prefix search, and stable ranking.
- [Eval Failure Aggregator](https://leetllm.com/practice/eval-failure-aggregator): Easy; 25 min; Evaluation; languages: python3, java; Aggregate eval run rows into stable pass-rate and error diagnostics.
- [SSE Event Parser](https://leetllm.com/practice/sse-event-parser): Medium; 35 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Parse chunked server-sent events while handling split lines, comments, and multiline data payloads.
- [Streaming Markdown Parser](https://leetllm.com/practice/streaming-markdown-parser): Medium; 35 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Parse streamed Markdown chunks into text, inline-code, and fenced-code tokens while preserving delimiter state.
- [Retry Backoff Planner](https://leetllm.com/practice/retry-backoff-planner): Easy; 25 min; Reliability; languages: python3, java; Plan retry delays with capped exponential backoff and explicit retryable error classes.
- [Tool Call Schema Validator](https://leetllm.com/practice/tool-call-schema-validator): Medium; 35 min; Agents; languages: python3, java; Validate tool call names and arguments before runtime execution.
- [Webhook Idempotency Receiver](https://leetllm.com/practice/webhook-idempotency-receiver): Medium; 35 min; Agents; languages: python3, java; Handle retried provider events with delivery dedupe, logical idempotency keys, and repo policy checks.
- [Model Fallback Router](https://leetllm.com/practice/model-fallback-router): Medium; 30 min; Serving; languages: python3, java; Route requests to the cheapest eligible healthy model with capability and quota checks.
- [PR Readiness Gate](https://leetllm.com/practice/pr-readiness-gate): Easy; 25 min; Agents; languages: python3, java; Evaluate a pull-request merge policy across required checks, review states, and required build artifacts.
- [Token Budget Ledger](https://leetllm.com/practice/token-budget-ledger): Medium; 35 min; Rate Limiting; languages: python3, java; Maintain rolling-window token spend per caller with expiry on every read and write path.
- [Batch Inference Scheduler](https://leetllm.com/practice/batch-inference-scheduler): Medium; 35 min; Serving; languages: python3, java; Batch requests by size or oldest-wait deadline while preserving FIFO order.
- [Streaming Token Assembler](https://leetllm.com/practice/streaming-token-assembler): Easy; 25 min; Streaming; languages: python3, java; Assemble interleaved streaming token deltas into complete message text.
- [Document Permission Filter](https://leetllm.com/practice/document-permission-filter): Medium; 30 min; Retrieval; languages: python3, java; Filter retrieval chunks by public, tenant, group, and private permissions before ranking.
- [Experiment Traffic Splitter](https://leetllm.com/practice/experiment-traffic-splitter): Medium; 30 min; Evaluation; languages: python3, java; Assign stable experiment variants using weighted deterministic buckets.
- [Prompt Section Extractor](https://leetllm.com/practice/prompt-section-extractor): Medium; 35 min; Parsing; languages: python3, java; Parse explicit prompt boundary markers while detecting outside text, duplicates, and unterminated sections.
- [Secret Redactor](https://leetllm.com/practice/secret-redactor): Easy; 25 min; Security; languages: python3, java; Redact common emails, bearer tokens, and API-key-shaped strings from log text.
- [Canary Metric Judge](https://leetllm.com/practice/canary-metric-judge): Medium; 35 min; Evaluation; languages: python3, java; Judge canary promotion with traffic, error-rate, latency, and quality thresholds.
